lesson_title: Why Your Ceiling Is Warmer Than Your Floor
hook_text: Put one thermometer on the floor and one on a high shelf. In winter, they can disagree by five degrees.
clip_script: Here is the secret: convection. Air next to the heater warms up. Its particles spread out, so it gets lighter for its size, and the cooler air around it pushes it upward. It hits the ceiling, spreads, cools, sinks down the far wall and slides back along the floor to the heater. Round and round. That loop is a convection current. It is why heaters belong near the floor, why your cat sleeps on top of the cupboard, and why smoke rises. Same loop at the beach: land heats faster, warm air rises, and the cool sea breeze rushes in to fill the gap.
visual_style: Whiteboard cross-section of a room with a heater and curved arrows looping up, across, down and back, two thermometers showing different readings; then the same loop drawn over a beach.
pacing: Quick hook, a smooth looping middle, a breezy finish.
